<header class="c-pagehead">
  <div class="c-wrap">
    <p class="c-eyebrow">Division · Population</p>
    <h1>Geospatial Health</h1>
    <p>
      Where illness falls, and why there. Bangladesh is one of the most
      climate-exposed and densely settled countries in the world, which makes
      place an unusually strong predictor of health here.
    </p>
  </div>
</header>

<section class="c-slab c-slab--paper">
  <div class="c-wrap">
    <div class="c-split">
      <div class="c-prose">

        <h2>Spatial epidemiology &amp; disease mapping</h2>
        <p>
          Cluster detection and disease mapping using GIS, applied to vector-borne
          transmission — dengue in particular — where the spatial signal arrives
          well before the case counts do.
        </p>

        <h2>Earth observation &amp; climate health</h2>
        <p>
          Satellite remote sensing, including NASA earth observation data, used to
          track temperature anomaly, precipitation, land cover change and
          particulate pollution as environmental determinants of health.
        </p>

        <h2>Healthcare accessibility</h2>
        <p>
          Spatial network analysis of physical access to tertiary care, emergency
          services and primary clinics across rural and urban Bangladesh — travel
          time rather than straight-line distance, since the two diverge sharply
          during flooding.
        </p>

        <h2>Environmental exposure</h2>
        <p>
          Mapping groundwater contamination and industrial pollutants against
          chronic disease prevalence, a question with a long and specific history
          in this country.
        </p>
